signals.text: These initiatives include our Community Music Day, Get Up & Dance, our partnership with Cuckfield Bookfest, termly sports festivals, Wednesday ‘open labs’ and school Shakespeare performances among others.

With nine wide ranging ensembles each week and over 80% of Year 3 and 4 pupils playing a musical instrument, Music runs through all parts of our school and we are inordinately proud of the pupils that have gone onto win Music Scholarships to schools including King’s Canterbury, Ardingly, Brighton College and Eton.
From ballet to street dance, modern to Charleston, our weekly clubs and curriculum sessions mean Dance is part of the rhythm of everyday life at Cumnor.

Guided by our expert staff, many of whom hold regional and national honours in their own right, all children will have regular opportunities to play, within school as well as externally in local and national events, festivals and fixtures.

pageCache.text:
Our next Open Week is 12th – 16th October 2026. We would be delighted to show you why Cumnor is such an exceptional experience.
Every moment, extraordinary
Cumnor House Sussex offers an outstanding contemporary education, built on our commitment to individual opportunity, excellence and community.
We nurture individual, unique potential and believe every moment is an opportunity to unlock exciting new possibilities. Every child belongs.
Every moment, extraordinary
Every moment, extraordinary
Preparing for the future
A Cumnor education prepares children for entry into the best senior schools in the country. Broad and rich, it is distinctly contemporary in its approach, designed to ignite a love of learning and lay foundations for life.
Preparing for the future
Discover Pupil Stories
Conscientious Achiever
Conscientious Achiever
Teddy
Dramatic Presence
Teddy joined Cumnor at the beginning of Year 5 and immediately stole our hearts. Coming from a Steiner school, this amazing young woman, with her gentle smile, tangible warmth and eagerness to learn has accelerated academically. Within a few weeks, she was on the stage with a lead role in the Year 5 musical, where we realised just what talent she had modestly hidden from the world.
To hear her sing, to see her eyes light up, to feel the joy and emotion of performance flow through her is just wonderful. She’s thrown herself into everything here, and brings a sense of peace and togetherness to her friendships. But the stage remains her happy place, and we love seeing her there too.
Aggie
Competitive Spirit
Aggie is full of potential energy. Around school, she is relaxed, easy-going, affable; immensely popular, she is loved for her non-judgemental heart and her slightly goofy humour. Quietly diligent and conscientious, she has secured a place at Brighton College, testimony to her growing academic confidence and her great attitude.
But then you put her onto the sports pitch, and suddenly she transforms. Tall, athletic, powerful, she is brave, she is competitive and she exudes talent. An A team player across all the sports, she is a genuine all-rounder at this stage, as accomplished in a technical sport such as cricket or hockey, as she is on the athletics track or football pitch. And yet, despite all the medals and personal accolades, she comes off the pitch and is immediately her humble, kind and thoughtful self.
Rafe
Exceptional Mind
Rafe has been with us since Nursery, and even back then, you could tell just how bright and driven he is. He has an exceptional mind, but more than that, he loves to learn, and just loves to get better. He relishes exams and tests, embraces discussion and debate, is interested in the world around him and how it works. He loves to ask the big questions. He happens also to be quick, athletic, sporty; he is kind and sensitive, relishing his role as a peer mentor; and he doesn’t mind donning a tutu and making fun of himself on stage at a recent Variety Show!
He’s an excellent Head Boy, full of insight, empathy and practicality. Most importantly, he is a good person with great values and a humble heart.
Mia
Nurturing Spirit
It can be hard for most children to move schools, especially when you are so young, but imagine coming out of ‘lockdown’, having lived on a tropical Island, only to arrive in Sussex at a British Prep! Such has been Mia’s journey, joining us, as she did, from Mauritius in 2022.
Not surprisingly, Mia was initially tentative and shy, and found some of the formalities of the classroom hard to adjust to. Yet, through the loving care and support of her form teachers and TAs, as well as the warmth and fun of her peers, you will now find her earnestly beavering away with the broadest of grins on her face.
In fact, she is perhaps one of the most emotionally intelligent children in the year, and carries with her a deeply nurturing spirit, the first to welcome any new child into the classroom.
Hugo
Young Entrepreneur
You will struggle to find a more willing, keen, enthusiastic learner than Hugo.
He is by nature diligent and very conscientious, and given his learning needs, he continues to show great perseverance and determination in all of his academic subjects. He is flourishing in our Kudos curriculum, where he has not only been able to demonstrate his skills and knowledge in different ways, but has also found opportunities such as our Entrepreneurship program that have harnessed his creativity and social intelligence, and earnt himself some money along the way!
Cheerful, eager, full of positivity and engagement, he is a much loved boy here at Cumnor. He has a fantastic attitude to life, always willing to put up his hand and ‘have a go’; he will certainly go a long way in life.
Nakiso
Positive Presence
Nakiso arrived in 2023 as one of our Foundation Scholars. The first thing you notice about her is her smile, and wherever she is around the Cumnor campus, she exudes positivity. She never takes the opportunities on offer here at Cumnor for granted, and is utterly wholehearted in everything she does. She is strong, conscientious and engaged, with a diligent heart and mind that means that her progress in all areas of school life has been rapid.
What Nakiso loves most about Cumnor are her friends, whom she blesses with her kindness, steadiness and loyalty. All children deserve a place to put down their roots and blossom, and that is just what Nakiso is doing.
Ethan
Quiet Confidence
Ethan is a quietly impressive young man. His growth in confidence, maturity and aspiration over the past two years has been astonishing, chiefly fuelled by his love for Performing Arts.
Ethan has weekly LAMDA lessons at school, and is a prominent member of many Cumnor music groups and choirs. His main instrument is the French Horn, but he also sings and is teaching himself the piano. He has thrown himself into Cumnor productions and his growing confidence has helped him secure offers from all three of the top Sussex senior schools he applied for. Bright, creative, imaginative, sensitive, kind, determined, self-reliant, we suspect he will be a star of the stage or screen in the future.
Matilda
Conscientious Achiever
Matilda is by nature very conscientious. In the classroom, her love of reading, her creativity and imagination, and her willingness to engage in new ideas and learning really shines through. She is mature, independent, but happy to collaborate.
Matilda is a keen contributor to all areas of Cumnor life, and has already hit some notable heights, whether it be a starring role as the Headmistress in our phenomenal Year 7 production of ‘School of Rock’, or bowling the critical over at Lords, helping to secure a bronze medal in the ECB National Finals.
Enthusiastic and curious, she literally brightens a room, and has a very positive influence on those around her, full of grace and warmth.

A vibrant community, there for everyone
Cumnor is more than the sum of its parts. What makes us more is our community. A home from home, where every family is welcomed, supported and celebrated.

Our next Open Week is 12th – 16th October 2026. We would be delighted to show you why Cumnor is such an exceptional experience.
Partnerships and values
We are committed to our enduring role in the community. Our doors are always open, and we warmly welcome all those who share in daily life at Cumnor.
Community
Community
Cumnor is part of the fabric of the local Sussex community. So, it matters that we are ready to serve this community and in so doing, discover the best in ourselves. This commitment does not stop at our gates; we are passionate about sharing our love of science, sport, reading and the Performing Arts, and work closely with local primary schools to improve access and inspire new generations.
These initiatives include our Community Music Day, Get Up & Dance, our partnership with Cuckfield Bookfest, termly sports festivals, Wednesday ‘open labs’ and school Shakespeare performances among others.
Follow us @cumnorhousesussex to find out more.
Philanthropy
Philanthropy
The Cumnor Foundation is the cornerstone of our fundraising and philanthropy. Dedicated to creating transformational bursaries, the Foundation is unique in covering the entire cost of a child’s education at an independent school for ten years from the ages of 8 to 18.
In less than ten years, The Cumnor Foundation has already made a mark, creating life-changing opportunities every year for local children with the potential, but otherwise not the means, to join Cumnor House Sussex.
The Cumnor Foundation
Fundraising
Fundraising
Driven by collective community effort, we support local causes that are close to our hearts, where our contribution can have real impact. Our ‘charities of the year’ are nominated by children, parents and staff.
Led by our generous parent body, our campaigns have raised over £150,000 in the past three years from much anticipated events including our Christmas Fair, Fireworks Night and Summer Fête. We also help to tackle food poverty in our local Sussex region through donations to local foodbanks as part of our Harvest celebrations.

Our next Open Week is 12th – 16th October 2026. We would be delighted to show you why Cumnor is such an exceptional experience.
Drama and Dance
Drama and Dance at Cumnor are more than just subjects; they are spaces for expression, discovery and joy.
Through our extensive Drama and Dance Programme, children learn to interact with others, becoming intuitive and agile communicators, and growing in self-belief.
From the very first steps in Reception to the final bow in Year 8, every child takes part in a journey that celebrates imagination, builds confidence, and nurtures creativity. Our belief is simple, but powerful; every child has a voice worth hearing and a story worth telling.
We have a duty as teachers to create memories. Our Drama Scholarship Programme supports students to reach ever higher and fulfil their potential. It has enabled our keenest and most talented pupils win Drama Scholarships to Brighton College, Worth, Eastbourne, Tonbridge, King’s Canterbury, Hurstpierpoint and Ardingly over the last few years.
Mrs Harris, Director of drama
Drama
Drama
Every single child from Reception to Year 8 will have the opportunity to perform in at least one of our 30+ events each year. From intimate coffee concerts and drama showcases, to seasonal concerts, variety shows, nativity plays, musicals and our annual set piece, the outdoor Shakespeare performance.
Whether their dream is to perform centre-stage, to design the set, create the stage make-up or be a sound or lighting technician, every child has an important role to play.
LAMDA
LAMDA
Drama at Cumnor opens doors, builds futures and creates lasting confidence. As part of our Performing Arts Programme, from Year 4 we offer the opportunity to work towards London Academy of Music and Dramatic Arts (LAMDA) examinations.
A wonderful way to learn important life skills, pupils take part in fun, imaginative and expressive lessons, encouraging confidence and the development of communication and physical awareness. Each grade encourages and challenges different aspects of text, language, creativity and vocal strength; inspiring young minds to discover their voice.
Dance
Dance
Our Dance provision continues to grow. From ballet to street dance, modern to Charleston, our weekly clubs and curriculum sessions mean Dance is part of the rhythm of everyday life at Cumnor. We believe in the discipline of dance and the skills it trains for life. We offer a range of classes in our purpose-built Dance Studio and collaborate with renowned dance companies such as ZooNation to widen our provision and increase its appeal to all our pupils.
Our commitment to the Performing Arts does not stop at the school gates; our love of the arts is something that we share with our wider community.
Matilda the Musical Jr
For 2026 a superb ensemble of Year 7 pupils threw themselves into the wonderful world of musical theatre with boundless energy, infectious curiosity and plenty of courage. It was an absolute triumph and we are delighted to have received five nominations by the National School Theatre Awards in recognition of this. You can read their detailed review here.

Our next Open Week is 12th – 16th October 2026. We would be delighted to show you why Cumnor is such an exceptional experience.
Music
The Music Department plays an important part in school life and is dedicated to engaging and inspiring pupils, building on their natural enthusiasm.
Music at Cumnor taps into children’s natural love of music and encourages them to explore further. We focus not just on technical knowledge, but help children to build their own musical language to express their thoughts and ideas.
Through weekly music lessons in our historic Music Barn, children develop an awareness of a wide range of musical genres and eras as well as the technical and theoretical knowledge to support their performing and composing skills.
With nine wide ranging ensembles each week and over 80% of Year 3 and 4 pupils playing a musical instrument, Music runs through all parts of our school and we are inordinately proud of the pupils that have gone onto win Music Scholarships to schools including King’s Canterbury, Ardingly, Brighton College and Eton.
The results speak for themselves and we are delighted to have been shortlisted by The Week School Guide 2025 for ‘Best for Music’! To be featured alongside two cathedral schools is testament to the strength of our Department.
I am delighted to have joined Cumnor this term and I am excited to bring my many years’ experience in professional music, particularly as a pianist and Musical Director on countless national tours and West End productions, to uphold and further develop the school’s incredibly high standards of performance.
With so many schools seeing a decline in the number of pupils learning orchestral instruments, developing our choirs and orchestra is of utmost priority. Our young people are the orchestra of the future – I hope we will boast an unrivalled range of orchestral musicians in a Music Department that thrives as the beating heart of the school.
Mr Cousins, Director of Music
The joy of learning
The joy of learning
Our Music provision comes in many shapes in sizes. From exploring and mastering a new instrument – from piano to harp, and electric guitar to gamelan – to all types of singing, as soloists, choristers and in musical theatre.
A busy calendar of events gives every child the chance to perform, from our informal coffee concerts to instrument-specific recitals, fully staged musicals and our seasonal showcases, Winter Wonderland and the Summer Serenade.
Community Music Day
Community Music Day
The highlight of the musical calendar is our ambitious Community Music Day. Hosted at Arundel Cathedral, it brings together professional and amateur musicians, children, and adults for an intensive one-day community music event.
For our inaugural event in 2023 we staged a wonderful production of ‘Noye’s Fludde’, followed by the rousing ‘Symphonic Adiemus’ in 2024. This year we returned with ‘Sacred Jazz’, featuring Chappell’s ‘The Daniel Jazz’, written in dedication to Cumnor in 1963. Involving all children from Year 3 to 5, the opportunity to have performed opera, an oratorio and jazz alongside professional and amateur musicians is unique within a prep school setting.

pageCache.pageTitle: Matilda the Musical Jr Reflections | Cumnor House Sussex
pageCache.text:
Our next Open Week is 12th – 16th October 2026. We would be delighted to show you why Cumnor is such an exceptional experience.
Matilda the Musical Jr Reflections
Every so often, something happens that feels so significant, that it elicits a wide variety of responses. I’ve tried to capture some of mine.
Fergus Llewellyn, Headmaster
At Cumnor, we often talk about moments. And when we talk about moments, we think of things that individuals might experience. The excitement of a child experiencing something new. The joy of a parent witnessing their child do something amazing.
What happened in our theatre last week feels like a moment for the whole community. A collective moment where we all felt something extraordinary had just happened. A moment where deep down we all knew we had witnessed something that would be spoken of for years. A moment where everybody in that space felt transported and transformed.
There is something truly beautiful in seeing talent shine. I have said many times that I believe all of our children are unique and wonderful; to see that wonderfulness in all its power and glory is truly special, and it takes a truly special talent to draw it out.
One of the unique things about drama, especially school drama, is that it becomes a collective experience. The whole year group are involved, and the whole school comes to watch.
One of the most powerful things about Matilda the Musical Jr was the fact that every single performer, and every single performance, was of the highest standard. Every child connected – with the music, with the moment, with each other. They were all utterly in it.
The energy was palpable, the teamwork extraordinary. That sense of connection is so rare.
Matilda is a play about a young girl finding her place in the world, and how the kind, affirming encouragement of the two women in her life allow her to find her voice. And when she finds her voice, others follow. That is exactly what we witnessed last week.
What last week also confirmed for me is that leading a school well means allowing the talent you have in your team to be liberated. Our Director of Drama, Charley Harris, has always had the conviction that she could create something very special, and she was right. Alongside, we built the team. Rob Cousins, as our Director of Music, with all his West End experience, was the perfect fit, and he added so much. Sam Taylor, as a young graduate, is full of talent and creativity, and perfectly balanced the group.
Everybody sensed that something special was happening; that something very important for those children, for the school, was about to take place. Our culture, the culture of aiming high and being kind, kicked in. Tim Freeman and our Maintenance team spent countless, dedicated hours creating set design to rival professional theatres, even building a swing! Barney J, a Year 8 DT Scholar, designed, programmed and operated the incredibly technical stage lighting. Over 25 staff volunteered to help with backstage, make up, front of house, catering……the list goes on.
I am proud of each and every one of our Year 7 children, of all that they have given, of the skills they have shown, of their teamwork, their attitude, and ultimately their performance. Ultimately, how do I feel?
I feel a deep sense of joy. Joy in the effect that the performance had on all who have seen it. Joy in the fact that our community has experienced the power of theatre. Joy that I’ve been able to stand at the back of a dark room and be part of it.

For 2026 a superb ensemble of Year 7 pupils threw themselves into the wonderful world of musical theatre with boundless energy, infectious curiosity and plenty of courage. It was an absolute triumph and we are delighted to have received five nominations by the National School Theatre Awards in recognition of this. You can read their detailed review here.

Music
The Music Department plays an important part in school life and is dedicated to engaging and inspiring pupils, building on their natural enthusiasm.
Music at Cumnor taps into children’s natural love of music and encourages them to explore further. We focus not just on technical knowledge, but help children to build their own musical language to express their thoughts and ideas.
Through weekly music lessons in our historic Music Barn, children develop an awareness of a wide range of musical genres and eras as well as the technical and theoretical knowledge to support their performing and composing skills.
With nine wide ranging ensembles each week and over 80% of Year 3 and 4 pupils playing a musical instrument, Music runs through all parts of our school and we are inordinately proud of the pupils that have gone onto win Music Scholarships to schools including King’s Canterbury, Ardingly, Brighton College and Eton.
The results speak for themselves and we are delighted to have been shortlisted by The Week School Guide 2025 for ‘Best for Music’! To be featured alongside two cathedral schools is testament to the strength of our Department.
I am delighted to have joined Cumnor this term and I am excited to bring my many years’ experience in professional music, particularly as a pianist and Musical Director on countless national tours and West End productions, to uphold and further develop the school’s incredibly high standards of performance.
With so many schools seeing a decline in the number of pupils learning orchestral instruments, developing our choirs and orchestra is of utmost priority. Our young people are the orchestra of the future – I hope we will boast an unrivalled range of orchestral musicians in a Music Department that thrives as the beating heart of the school.
Mr Cousins, Director of Music
The joy of learning
The joy of learning
Our Music provision comes in many shapes in sizes. From exploring and mastering a new instrument – from piano to harp, and electric guitar to gamelan – to all types of singing, as soloists, choristers and in musical theatre.
A busy calendar of events gives every child the chance to perform, from our informal coffee concerts to instrument-specific recitals, fully staged musicals and our seasonal showcases, Winter Wonderland and the Summer Serenade.
Community Music Day
Community Music Day
The highlight of the musical calendar is our ambitious Community Music Day. Hosted at Arundel Cathedral, it brings together professional and amateur musicians, children, and adults for an intensive one-day community music event.
For our inaugural event in 2023 we staged a wonderful production of ‘Noye’s Fludde’, followed by the rousing ‘Symphonic Adiemus’ in 2024. This year we returned with ‘Sacred Jazz’, featuring Chappell’s ‘The Daniel Jazz’, written in dedication to Cumnor in 1963. Involving all children from Year 3 to 5, the opportunity to have performed opera, an oratorio and jazz alongside professional and amateur musicians is unique within a prep school setting.

Art and design
We value art highly at Cumnor, inspiring all our budding artists to express themselves freely, and with confidence. Our reputation for excellence is founded in nurturing individual creativity.
We are firing young imaginations, nurturing individual creativity and developing technical skills for the future.
We challenge children to develop their own, original ideas, and support them with the practical elements that enable them to become technically proficient.
Raising the bar, and drawing on her background in textile design, our dedicated Head of Art encourages children to work with a wide range of materials and processes in both 2D and 3D media, including sketching, painting, printmaking, textiles, ceramics, sculpture and animation.
A sketchbook work culture sits at the heart of our approach, encouraging everyone to keep art journals and to instil a lifelong love of drawing.
Our distinct approach is consistently recognised through the number of Art Scholarships our children have secured at a range of senior schools including Brighton College, King’s Canterbury, Tonbridge, Eastbourne and Hurst.
Kerrie Pope, Head of Art
Joined by inspirational artists and art educators, our children regularly enjoy masterclasses, all taking place in the Art Studio, a dedicated, light-filled space with a mezzanine area for our Scholars’ enrichment program. We also hold an annual exhibition of our Scholars’ work to much acclaim.
Beautifully curated, the standard and variety of work was breath-taking.

Design technology
Practical and future-focused, DT at Cumnor is designed for a fast-changing world where agility and creativity is key.
Under visionary leadership, DT at Cumnor has gone from strength to strength. We work with real life problems and projects relevant for today’s world – with sustainability in mind.
Housed in our dedicated STEM facility, our state-of-the-art DT lab is unrivalled in a prep school setting and is a hive of activity, innovation and creative confidence. With our open-door policy, pupils can drop in whenever they have a moment – so break times are never quiet!
Our DT program focuses on giving pupils the technical knowledge and skills to bring their ideas to life. Building their understanding of resistant materials, graphics, electronics and computer-aided design and manufacture using lasers, we give them the tools to innovate.
This practical, future-focused approach not only brings unusual agility in problem-solving to all our children. It has also brought the school significant scholarship success, too, with no less than five DT scholarships in the last year alone, to leading senior schools including Brighton College and King’s Canterbury.
Tori Bramly, Head of DT
A racing start
A racing start
Now a regular fixture in Cumnor’s STEM calendar, our annual go-kart project pits together teams of Year 6 pupils to dismantle and re-build a working kart, then test and race it. Challenging their scientific and mathematical knowledge throughout, the project culminates in a competitive race.
This year it was off to Goodwood to hone their driving skills as they competed in the drag race, slalom, chicane sprint, lap of champions and pit-stop challenge.

Destinations and scholarships
We are an outstanding school that produces dynamic and creative young people, well prepared and ready for their next steps, confident of who they are and what they can do.
We are proud to prepare our Year 8 leavers for a range of destination schools, including all of Sussex’s outstanding independent senior schools, and the very best weekly and full boarding schools across the country.
We are a non-selective school. Notwithstanding, our pupils have secured a remarkable 163 scholarship awards over the past five years with 72% of this year’s leavers winning scholarships including 6 Performing Arts, 11 Academic, 7 Sport and 6 Creative Arts. We are also truly independent, sending our children onto 52 different senior schools in the last ten years.
We put this success down to the individualised attention that every child in our school receives. It is what sets us apart, and it is what enables all our pupils to achieve such outstanding results.
2025 Leavers Destination Senior Schools
Reflections from Cumnor parents
Senior school pathways
Senior school pathways
Choosing a senior school starts in Year 5 with a talk for all parents. After this, we arrange private one-to-one meetings to discuss individual choices, longlisting, shortlisting and then final choices.
When the time comes to look at future schools, we offer personalised advice and targeted support, founded on longstanding relationships with our senior school partners.
Fergus Llewellyn, Headmaster
You are in very capable hands. We advise you at every stage of the process including personalised, thorough and targeted academic support.

Our next Open Week is 12th – 16th October 2026. We would be delighted to show you why Cumnor is such an exceptional experience.
Welcome to Pre-Prep
The early years are not just a stepping stone. They are the foundation on which everything else is built, and we believe they should be nothing short of extraordinary.
The motivation to learn is a powerful force and one we champion and channel without limit. We encourage children to be confident in asking questions, fearless in making mistakes and excited and ambitious when branching out to reach their potential.
Ours is an education rooted in academic rigour, tailored to each child, creativity, wellbeing and unforgettable childhood experiences. From STEM experiments and specialist sport, to bringing the house down in our state-of-the-art theatre, children are encouraged to explore their talents and passions.
Fundamental to our success is the value we place on parent partnership and individualised care. We see progression at Cumnor as a collective endeavour; you can see and feel the strength of our community on a daily basis.
As both Head of Pre-Prep and a parent, I know first-hand what a special place this is. If this is the kind of beginning you want for your child, we would be delighted to welcome you.
Sarah Gibson
Head of Pre-Prep and Nursery
Discover a learning adventure
Discover a learning adventure
The Early Years at Cumnor are the stepping stones where early learnings are reinforced, and new habits are created for life. We think of it as an adventure, and like all adventures, every path will be different.
Experience & expertise
Experience & expertise
We are experts in child development and pastoral care is central to all we do. We provide highly individualised care so our children feel understood. Each child is noticed, every moment is meaningful, and a strong foundation for life is built. From this, their learning will flourish.

Sport at Cumnor
Regardless of ability, sport has the power to permeate us all. We believe that sport shapes character, builds community, and creates values that last a lifetime.
We are transforming what Prep school sport can look like. By inspiring every pupil to discover their individual opportunity, develop resilience, and lead with integrity — on and off the field — we are creating a programme that prioritises both enjoyment and excellence.
Our approach recognises that every child has different interests, strengths, and preferences, and we are committed to providing opportunities that ensure every moment is extraordinary. Through contemporary coaching methodologies, we nurture individual excellence within a supportive environment where every pupil can flourish. For those on an elite sporting pathway, our programme is centred around developing well-rounded, high-performing young athletes, with a strong emphasis on physical and psychological excellence.
Our teams have won a range of national and regional honours over the past five years and many of our children are linked into key regional pathways. Our approach has also seen our children secure a remarkable number scholarships to the top sporting senior schools in the country including Millfield, Tonbridge and Brighton College.
By embracing our vision and living our values, sport at Cumnor is enjoyable, inclusive, and developmental. By prioritising choice without compromising on standards, we inspire pupils to fully engage, challenge themselves, and embrace opportunities for growth.
Charlotte Collard-Rowe, Director of Sport
Sport for everyone
Sport for everyone
Ours is an inclusive, challenging, and rewarding sporting environment where all pupils are encouraged to pursue personal excellence, contribute meaningfully to their teams and enjoy the experiences and lessons that sport provides.
Sport is about more than competition — it is a journey of individual excellence and community pride.
For some this might mean competing at a regional or national level. For others it will be developing new skills and enjoying being part of a team.
Variety is key
Variety is key
Everyone is included. Guided by our expert staff, many of whom hold regional and national honours in their own right, all children will have regular opportunities to play, within school as well as externally in local and national events, festivals and fixtures. Needless to say, our Cumnor community will always be there, ready to support and celebrate our competitors.
Our range of sports include hockey, football, rugby, netball, cricket, tennis, golf, equestrian and athletics. Our broader options programme includes badminton, strength training, golf, hiking and dance.
Whatever the event, we are wholehearted in our participation, and we have a track record to show for it. Every pupil is part of an ongoing legacy.

Bursary opportunities
We are delighted to offer the following bursaries – our Foundation Scholarships from Year 4 to Year 8 and our music tuition assistance, awarded in recognition of our commitment to the Performing Arts and musical excellence.
Foundation scholarships
Foundation scholarships
Through the Cumnor Foundation*, we fund bursaries – our Foundation Scholarships – which cover up to 100% of school fees and extras from Year 4 (aged 8+) to Year 8 (aged 13).
Applications are invited from local families for whom independent school education would otherwise be out of reach financially. Candidates should currently be in Year 3, performing towards the top of their class and curious to explore and deepen their talents, whether that be in the classroom, on the sports pitch or on the stage.
We help our bursary families to identify the best senior school for their child and facilitate this move for Year 9 entry, ideally with continued financial assistance at a similar level under that school’s own bursary programme.
Applications for Year 4 entry in September 2027 will open in December 2026 or January 2027.
*Charity No: 1168316
Music tuition bursary
Music tuition bursary
Children achieving the following grades are eligible to apply for paid tuition for up to two instruments, provided they are taught at the school. In the case of a music theory candidate achieving Grade 5, one of their instrumental studies at school will be supported. The Headmaster may also award discretionary financial assistance for music lessons to children in Year 3 to Year 5. These awards are reviewed annually.

Relocating to Sussex
Cumnor offers the best of both worlds. Located in the beautiful Sussex countryside between the South Downs and the Ashdown Forest, we are just a 15-minute drive from Haywards Heath and East Grinstead, for easy travel to London and Brighton.
Many of our families have moved from London or further afield. We are always delighted to support you during this process.
We will happily put you in touch with others who have already been through a similar move and connect you with your child’s cohort through our Year Group Reps. Prospective parents are also most welcome to join our events, whether that is watching a performance in our Theatre or attending our social events.
Our Head of Pre-Prep, Sarah Gibson, recently moved along with her family from London and shares her experiences here.
